- `import { chromium } from 'playwright'` (already installed). `page.goto(url, { waitUntil: 'load', timeout: 60000 })` — NOT `networkidle`, Storybook's HMR websocket never goes idle and it will time out. Follow with `await page.waitForTimeout(1500)`.
- Story URL shape: `http://localhost:6006/iframe.html?id=<story-id>&viewMode=story`. Get real story IDs via `curl -s http://localhost:6006/index.json`.
- Real computed styles: `page.evaluate(() => getComputedStyle(el))` inside the browser context, on the actual visible text/icon element, not a wrapping container — one of the three bugs just found was exactly this mistake (checking a container's style instead of the element that actually renders).

Your scope: `ZimmInlineMessage` (`overrides/app/components/ui-kits/atoms/zimmInlineMessage/`) — all three variants (`error`, `warning`, `success`). The `success` variant (used for the discount label) already went through a real Playwright measurement round during its own original build (commit 9) and should be the most reliable of the three — still worth a fresh confirmation, but the `error` and `warning` variants have NOT had that same treatment and are higher risk. Read `.runs/SFCC-11/figma-reference/warnings-shown.md`, `warnings-hidden.md`, and `stacked-error-messages.md` first for the exact specs (icon only on `warning` — `Icon_info_solid` — never on `error` or `success`; `text.muted`/`#969696` colour; exact copy strings).

Measure live for each variant (Storybook story IDs will include something like `commerce-productitem--with-error-message`/`--with-warning-message`, plus `zimmInlineMessage`'s own stories — check `index.json` for the exact set):
1. The actual rendered text's computed font-size/weight/line-height/colour for each variant — compare against the specific Figma-documented value per variant, not a single shared assumption.
2. Whether the icon actually renders for `warning` and does NOT render for `error`/`success` — confirm by checking real DOM presence, not just reading the component's conditional.
3. The icon's real rendered size/position if present.
4. Any spacing between the icon and text, and between stacked messages when more than one renders on the same line item (product-item has a story combining `discountLabel` + `message` — measure the real gap between them).

For each finding: state the exact measured number vs. the exact spec'd number, the file/line it comes from, and whether it's CONFIRMED or PLAUSIBLE. If everything checks out clean, say so — but only after measuring. Report back in text, concise — don't paste raw script output, just the findings.

import React from 'react';
import { chakra, useMultiStyleConfig } from '@chakra-ui/react';
import { ZimmIcon } from 'app/components/ui-kits/atoms/zimmIcon';

const ZIMM_INLINE_MESSAGE_RECIPE = 'ZimmInlineMessage';

export type ZimmInlineMessageProps = {
  /**
   * Colour/severity only — this atom never decides which one applies. A caller may legitimately
   * pass `variant="warning"` for copy whose own requirement text uses the word "error" (the cart
   * max-quantity message is exactly this case) — see zimmInlineMessage.css.ts's own docblock for
   * why that's a deliberate word-vs-severity reconciliation, not a mismatch to fix here.
   *
   * `success` added SFCC-795 plan step 3.3 (Marcel's direct Figma inspector pull, 2026-09-18) for
   * the cart-line discount label ("20% off applied") — see this component's own docblock below.
   */
  variant: 'error' | 'warning' | 'success';
  /**
   * Message copy, rendered verbatim. This atom never derives, hardcodes, or paraphrases copy — a
   * caller supplies the already-resolved string (e.g. "This item is unavailable", "Quantity
   * unavailable in this size", "Maximum purchase quantity reached for this size" — SFCC-795
   * §11.2 exact copy).
   */
  text: string;
  /**
   * Overrides the root element's `data-testid`, defaulting to the pre-existing hardcoded
   * `'zimm-inline-message'` — every caller that omits this keeps that exact default, unchanged.
   * Added SFCC-795 plan step 3.3: a single cart line can now render both a discount label
   * (`variant="success"`) and an error/warning `message` at once (product-item/index.tsx), so two
   * `ZimmInlineMessage` instances can appear on one line — without a distinct testid per instance,
   * `getByTestId('zimm-inline-message')` would match both and throw.
   */
  dataTestId?: string;
};

/**
 * Atom — cart-line inline status message (SFCC-795 §11.2, plan step 3.2). Presentation only:
 * renders whatever `variant`/`text` it is given and never determines availability itself.
 * OOS/partial-OOS detection is SFCC-282's, "Unavailable" detection is SFCC-796's — both
 * later-sprint tickets this component does not, and should not, anticipate. No low-stock variant
 * exists in `ZimmInlineMessageProps['variant']` — a separate requirement explicitly forbids
 * low-stock messaging at the cart level (see zimmInlineMessage.css.ts).
 *
 * `aria-live="polite"` matches the same treatment this codebase already gives another transient,
 * non-input cart-line status value — ZimmQuantityStepper's own quantity display (its `value`
 * part, zimmQuantityStepper/index.tsx) carries the identical `aria-live="polite"` treatment — so
 * a shopper using assistive tech is told about a message that appears/changes after their own
 * action, without requiring focus to move to it.
 *
 * SFCC-795 rework (Marcel's own visual checkpoint against the real Figma file): the `warning`
 * variant renders a leading `info-solid` icon, `error` never does — confirmed against 3 real
 * cart-item instances in Figma file QQ427wHWEUjsjP7H8v48Rs: the two error-copy states (FULLY OOS
 * node 9323-101979, PARTIAL OOS node 9323-98397) have no icon in their message sub-tree; the
 * warning-copy state's own "Cart Item" instance (9323:106685 — one of 5 per-item rows inside the
 * "WARNINGS SHOWN" frame's "Cart-item-group", not that frame's separate SFCC-404
 * "Cart-level-messages" sibling — see zimmInlineMessage.css.ts for the full parent-chain
 * citation) does. The icon is `aria-hidden` — the
 * message's own text plus `aria-live` already carry the full meaning to assistive tech, so the
 * icon is a purely visual (sighted-only) reinforcement of a severity already conveyed by colour
 * and copy, not an independent piece of information.
 *
 * SFCC-795 rework, part 2 (Marcel's direct Figma inspector pull for the discount-label node,
 * 2026-09-18): a third variant, `success`, renders the cart-line discount label ("20% off
 * applied", product-item/index.tsx's `discountLabel` prop). That element used to be a bespoke
 * `<Text>` styled to match the WRONG Figma node (item-variant.css.ts's `colourSize` part, a
 * different, medium-weight node); the real pulled node is `color:
 * var(--alias-color-text-success, #2D5A3D); font-size: var(--brand-font-size-300, 12px);
 * font-weight: 400; line-height: var(--brand-font-lineHeight-450, 18px)` — "Default/Caption", the
 * exact same regular-weight 12px/18px node family `error`/`warning` already render, coloured with
 * this codebase's own `status.success` token (byte-identical to the pulled hex — see
 * zimmInlineMessage.css.ts's own docblock for the token chain). Confirmed directly with Marcel:
 * `success` carries no icon, same as `error` — the icon condition below is unchanged and
 * `'success'` correctly falls through it.
 *
 * @param props see ZimmInlineMessageProps
 */
export const ZimmInlineMessage = ({ variant, text, dataTestId = 'zimm-inline-message' }: ZimmInlineMessageProps) => {
  const styles = useMultiStyleConfig(ZIMM_INLINE_MESSAGE_RECIPE, { variant });

  return (
    <chakra.div __css={styles.root} aria-live="polite" data-testid={dataTestId}>
      {variant === 'warning' && <ZimmIcon type="info-solid" size="md" aria-hidden />}
      <chakra.p __css={styles.text}>{text}</chakra.p>
    </chakra.div>
  );
};
